 Order

Dated this the 3rd day of October, 2024 This Criminal Miscellaneous Case has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, by the petitioners, to quash Annexure B Final Report and all further proceedings in C.C.No.996/2018 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-1, Chengannur, arose out of Crime No.762/2017 of Chengannur police station,
Alappuzha District.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-1, Chengannur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioners herein are accused Nos.1 and 2 in the above case.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned counsel appearing for the 2 nd respondent/de facto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the relevant records.

3. In this matter, the prosecution case is that, the 1st petitioner/1st accused herein, who married the de facto complainant in the year 2001, while both of them had been living as husband and wife at the matrimonial home, at 11.35 a.m. on 15.4.2017, the 1 st accused, after seeing a CRL.MC NO. 1810 OF 2022 3 2024:KER:73715 photograph of the de facto complainant along with another office staff,
slapped on the cheek of the de facto complainant, caught hold on her nose, put her down, and beat on her navel.
The allegation against the 2 nd petitioner/2nd accused is that, the 2nd accused abetted the same.
Accordingly, the prosecution alleges commission of offences punishable under Sections 323, 341 and 498A r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

4. While seeking quashment of the above proceedings, the learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the marriage in between the 1 st accused and the de facto complainant solemnized 16 years before the date of occurrence.
In fact, no issues in between them till the date of occurrence.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, as per the narration in the FIS itself, the allegation is that, when the husband noticed the photograph of the de facto complainant along with another office staff, which was taken, when the de facto complainant along with the office staff went for a tour during 2014.
It is submitted that, questioning of the same by the 1 st accused and the altercation thereafter, led to registration of this crime.
Therefore, the offences alleged by the prosecution, would not attract against accused Nos.1 and 2 and in such view of the matter, the quashment sought for, is liable to succeed.

5. Opposing quashment of the entire proceedings as against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2, the learned counsel appearing for the 2 nd respondent/de facto complainant would submit that, in the FIS, specific overt act stated against the 1st accused and there is allegation against the 2nd accused that she also engaged in using threatening words against the de facto complainant and as the outcome of the same, the 1 st accused manhandled her.
Therefore, quashment is liable to fail.

6. On perusal of the FIS, the prosecution case is that, the 1st petitioner/1st accused herein, who married the de facto complainant in the year 2001, while both of them had been living as husband and wife at the matrimonial home, at 11.35 a.m. on 15.4.2017, the 1st accused, after seeing a photograph of the de facto complainant along with another office staff, slapped on the cheek of the de facto complainant, caught hold on her nose, put her down, and beat on her navel.

The allegation against the 2 nd CRL.MC NO. 1810 OF 2022 5 2024:KER:73715 nd nd petitioner/2 accused is that,
the 2 accused abetted the same.

Thus, the prosecution records would show prima facie materials to Mohammed Raffi vs State Of Kerala on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30944946/
2 proceed against the 1 st petitioner/1st accused.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as the 2 nd petitioner/2nd accused is concerned, even though there is allegation that, the 2 nd accused also engaged in using threatening words against the de facto complainant and as the outcome of the same, the 1 st accused manhandled her, no overt acts specifically stated against the 2nd accused.

That apart, in the FIS itself, it is stated that, when the 1st accused manhandled the de facto complainant, the 2nd accused intervened to save her and the 1st accused pushed away the mother and slapped on the cheek of the de facto complainant.

7. On perusal of the records, prima facie case is made out against the 1st petitioner/1st accused,
warranting trial and therefore, quashment sought for by the 1 st petitioner/1st accused, is liable to fail.

Since there is no specific allegation against the 2 nd petitioner/2nd accused and she made an attempt to save the de facto complainant, the offences alleged against the 2nd accused are not made out, prima facie and therefore, quashment prayer, at the CRL.MC NO. 1810 OF 2022 6 2024:KER:73715 nd nd instance of the 2 petitioner/2 accused, is liable to succeed.
In the result, this petition is allowed in part.

Accordingly, Annexure B Final Report and all further proceedings as against the 2nd petitioner/2nd accused in C.C.No.996/2018 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-1, Chengannur, arose out of Crime No.762/2017 of Chengannur police station, Alappuzha District, stand quashed, while dismissing the quashment prayer at the option of the 1st petitioner/1st accused.
